mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -28.1% to -7.1%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend continues linearly over the next four weeks, producing positive net change in RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 21 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in week t+4w is lower than RETAIL_REC in week t-0w, or the week-on-week improvement rate decelerates to zero or negative for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen consistently from -5.6% to +13.0% over four weeks, signaling restored confidence in essential-goods shopping. This confidence spillover drives discretionary retail visits upward over the next four weeks as consumers normalize out-of-home activity patterns.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5% in either of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in at least 3 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed (-8.1% in t-0w) despite four-week improvement. When TRANSIT mobility fails to recover above -5%, commuting-dependent retail clusters remain suppressed. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks as the absence of transit-anchored foot traffic persists.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -5% for the next two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -8.1% in t-0w despite 25.6 point improvement
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility exceeds -3% in week t+1w or t+2w, or RETAIL_REC increases in 3 or more of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has surged to +62.4% (t-0w), indicating strong outdoor-activity preference. When PARKS exceeds +60% and RETAIL_REC remains below -5%, consumers are substituting outdoor recreation for indoor retail. This substitution effect will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds +60% AND RETAIL_REC remains below -5%
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below +50% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -41.4% to -17.1% over four weeks, signaling partial return to office routines. When WORKPLACES exceeds -15%, weekday retail activity near employment centers increases. This effect will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as workplace-adjacent shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 24.3 points over four weeks to -17.1%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -20% in either of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines in 3 or more of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has normalized from +6.6% to -0.1% over four weeks, indicating reduced stay-at-home behavior. Simultaneously, TRANSIT remains severely depressed at -8.1%. When RESIDENTIAL normalizes but TRANSIT does not recover proportionally, mobility is shifting to private transport, reducing retail foot traffic in transit-dependent zones. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL within -2% to +2% AND TRANSIT below -5%
failure_condition: TRANSIT exceeds -3% within two weeks, or RESIDENTIAL rises above +3%, or RETAIL_REC increases in 3 or more of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has reached +13.0% and PARKS at +62.4%, indicating strong outdoor and essential-goods activity. This pattern is consistent with seasonal shift toward outdoor recreation and essential shopping. RETAIL_REC will continue recovering as seasonal factors support discretionary spending over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS show strong positive values
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5% or PARKS falls below +40% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines in 3 or more of the next 4 weeks.

When both employment-center and transit-hub mobility remain below -5%, the structural conditions for retail recovery are absent. RETAIL_REC will stagnate or decline over the next four weeks despite recent marginal improvements.

evidence_refs: fact:Both remain significantly depressed despite four-week improvements
